label: prf:u1-equivariant-reduction
title: Proof of u1 equivariant reduction
html:
Proof sketch. Using the spherical parametrisation of def:exceptional-divisor, the \mathrm{U}(1) action is \psi \mapsto \psi + \alpha, leaving \phi fixed. Quotienting by \psi identifies orbits with \phi \in [0,\pi]; the two fixed points \phi = 0, \pi (the poles) collapse the \psi fibre to a point, while over \phi \in (0, \pi) the fibre is isomorphic to S^1 with phase coordinate \psi. \mathrm{U}(1)-equivariant observables therefore descend to sections of the associated phase-S^1 bundle over (0, \pi), which in the commutative limit is trivialisable to give a single global phase coordinate \varphi \in S^1. \square

Scope of the claim. The statement does not say the geometric fibre \mathcal{S}_p itself collapses --- it remains \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \cong S^2. What collapses is the \mathrm{U}(1)-invariant observable algebra, which reduces to functions on S^1 modulo the two polar fixed points. The physical interpretation of this S^1 as the single \mathrm{U}(1) phase tube is recorded in rem:u1-phase-tube.
